query: Consider the following context: The combination of elevated temperature and tribo-corrosion leads to the accelerated degradation of structural components used in many extreme environments. Recently developed high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with multiple principal elements have the potential for superior degradation resistance compared with presently used structural alloys. In that context, which material can be used for superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: An equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) will exhibit superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance compared to conventional structural alloys in high‐temperature, molten salt environments.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeMnNi HEA prepared in its as-cast (or homogenized) state with a uniform FCC solid-solution microstructure.
generation.intervention: Exposure to high-temperature conditions (>400 °C) in a corrosive environment (e.g., molten MgNaK chloride mixture) combined with sliding (tribological) contact.
generation.conditions: Operating in a molten salt environment typical of concentrating solar power (CSP) systems, where elevated temperature and mechanical sliding stresses are present.
generation.structural_mediator: The uniformly distributed elements in the FCC solid-solution structure that resist phase segregation and local elemental depletion.
generation.mechanism: The high configurational entropy of the HEA stabilizes a homogeneous microstructure that minimizes localized corrosion sites and suppresses the rapid dissolution of key elements (such as Cr). This stable structure, when subjected to combined tribological and corrosive attack, is expected to exhibit lower overall material loss and more uniform wear characteristics.
generation.predicted_outcome: Under the given conditions, the CoCrFeMnNi HEA is predicted to demonstrate lower mass loss and a more consistent wear track morphology relative to conventional alloys like 316H stainless steel.
generation.baseline: Performance metrics (mass loss, wear track damage) of conventional alloys (e.g., 316H stainless steel) under identical high-temperature tribo-corrosive testing conditions.
generation.boundary: The degree of improved performance may be sensitive to processing histories and the precise operating parameters (such as temperature, salt composition, and contact stresses). Uncertainty remains regarding the long-term effect of possible selective elemental dissolution (e.g., Mn loss) under sustained tribo-corrosion cycling.
generation.uncertainty: While the FCC solid-solution structure and corrosion resistance of CoCrFeMnNi HEA are well documented, its specific performance under simultaneous sliding wear and molten salt corrosion requires further experimental validation, particularly regarding the balance between protective Cr retention and potential Mn depletion.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare samples of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA and 316H stainless steel. Expose both sample sets to a high-temperature molten MgNaK chloride environment (>400 °C) under controlled sliding contact to simulate tribo-corrosion conditions. Monitor the samples over a defined period.
measurements: Wear track morphology and dimensions (using microscopy)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the CoCrFeMnNi HEA does not demonstrate at least a 20% lower mass loss rate and improved wear track uniformity compared to 316H stainless steel under these conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract The corrosion behavior of the FCC Cr 18 Mn 27 Fe 27.5 Ni 27.5 high entropy alloy (HEA) after exposure to molten FLiBe salt at 700 °C for 1000 hours, has been investigated. Results show that the HEA lost a higher mass compared to the reference 316 H stainless steel due to the dissolution of Mn into the molten salt. The loss of Mn from the alloy appeared to discourage the dissolution of Cr in the molten fluoride salts which is widely recognized as the mechanism of corrosion degradation. Thermal exposure at 700 °C for 1000 hours also led to the precipitation of an additional BCC phase Cr 67 Fe 13 Mn 18.5 Ni 1.5 , which was confirmed by CALPHAD predictions. Subject terms: Structural materials, Metals and alloys

Unlike other conventional alloys based on a “principal element,” high-entropy alloy (HEA) is a unique material that maintains a random solid solution structure without forming intermetallic compounds in operating temperatures due to its high configurational entropy [1] – [3] . It also has outstanding physical and chemical properties, which makes it a potential replacement for traditional metallic materials, and it has recently been referred to as a multi-principal element alloy (MPEA) or compositionally concentrated alloy (CCA) [4] – [9] .

As attention in HEAs increases, many studies have been conducted to explore its mechanical, physical and chemical properties [10] – [15] . In particular, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, which was the first developed HEA, is the most studied because of its excellent combination of tensile strength and elongation along with excellent fracture toughness and corrosion resistance [6] , [16] – [21] . However, despite the advantages of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, many issues arise owing to its low yield strength and costly and complex thermomechanical processing (i.e., multiple casting → hot rolling → homogenization → cold rolling → annealing → cutting, etc.
